notes: Banked 18-22 credits clicking for money for many turns while holding uninstalled cards and no killer, re-ran a known Vampyronassa; ended a turn with 0 cards against Personal Evolution with an advanced remote and was flatlined on the score.

Won, but clicked for credits at 10-20 credits for many early turns, twice paid 4 to put advancement counters on The Holo Man itself, and scored slowly against a broke, locked-out Runner sitting on dozens of tags.

Ran an unchanged R&D three or four times a turn re-accessing the same top card (hitting Behold! three times in one turn for 6 tags), sat at 0 credits for most of the game, and stayed tagged against NBN until End of the Line flatlined them.
Coherent plan: Trojan Horse killed the breaker, a well-iced remote scored three Send a Message, and advancing ice was used for Built to Last credits; only minor slack clicks.
Fast, sensible pressure on R&D then HQ, shuffling programs into the stack to steal two Degree Mills and winning on turn 8; spending clicks clearing NBN tags was reasonable.

For about 13 turns it did nothing but click twice for credits and spend them trashing a resource, sitting at 0 credits with no remote and no scoring; Bellona was eventually stolen from a weakly iced HQ.

Long aimless game: hosted Audrey, Botulus and Simulchip on Bling so they were trashed, clicked for credits with nothing to do, ran Archives nearly every turn and ignored R&D until turn 23; won only because the Corp was very passive.
Clicked for credits at 11-15 credits instead of drawing or contesting the remote; after net damage left a tiny grip, kept running R&D into Personal Evolution and Fujii and was flatlined on the steal.

Left R&D unprotected all game and installed almost no ice, spent turns repeatedly paying to trash resources down to 1 credit, and let the Runner take 8 points from R&D without ever building a scoring server.

Won with three Send a Message, but very slowly: it hoarded 20-40 credits, played double Government Subsidy while already rich and spent many clicks advancing ice; losing Above the Law to Inside Job was unlucky.

After an early Fujii score it stalled for about 12 turns, clicking for credits up to 60+ and installing assets without advancing its agenda plan; it won by a Phật Gioan flatline on a False Lead bait rather than by any plan.
Steady R&D pressure through cheap Ping, and good use of Trick Shot to hit the remote; some repeat HQ runs into Behold! and a risky final run through two Tsarevnas, but the plan worked.

Kept installing agendas behind the single Mestnichestvo that Matryoshka had already broken, giving up three agendas on consecutive turns, then clicked for credits for five turns without punishing a heavily tagged Runner.

Spent around ten turns re-running an unchanged R&D at 0 credits, passed whole turns doing nothing, then repeatedly ran through Unsmiling Tsarevna with 1-2 cards, piling up tags until End of the Line flatlined them.

Won with timely R&D steals, but gave up Aumakua to steal and was then stuck against Tree Line for many turns, facechecked a three-ice remote losing Cezve and WAKE, and spent many clicks on low-value Archives and HQ runs.
Against Chastushka's sabotage it binned two Stoke the Embers from HQ into an unprotected Archives, handing over 4 points; otherwise it scored steadily behind Ping against a Runner with no breakers.
Efficient: built Aumakua and money and then hit R&D for three 3-point agendas by turn 9; WAKE's meat damage on a tiny grip was a minor oddity.
Clicked for credits at 13-21 credits for many turns and never installed agendas, letting HQ flood with two Fujii and Regenesis behind one Anansi, which the Runner took to win.

Left Phoneutria unrezzed on R&D on turn 1 with enough credits, then spent its money on Oppo Research, letting the Runner steal See How They Run and Fujii; it recovered and flatlined the Runner with Phoneutria and Bladderwort.

For ten turns it ran an unchanged R&D four times a turn, then spent turns clicking for credits up to 28 without installing anything, and ignored a dozen undefended remotes until turn 20; it won only because the Corp never scored.
